editorial.verdict: The 14CG754 is the budget 2/3/4-thread serger with differential feed, rolled hem and a free arm, sold under a "Commercial Grade" label that describes the marketing, not the machine.
editorial.whoFor: A first serger buyer who wants 2-thread capability, differential feed and a free arm at the lowest price with a 25-year Singer head warranty.
editorial.skipIf: You want a brighter light, easier looper access, or a current model; the 14HD854 is Singer's own successor at a small premium.

faqs.a: Not officially. Singer's page is still live and retailers list it, but one dealer says the Heavy Duty 14HD854 replaces it and several listings show out of stock.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the 14CG754 and the 14HD854?
faqs.a: Both are 2/3/4-thread 1,300 spm sergers. Singer gives the 14HD854 a larger cutting knife, a stronger motor and a brighter light, and the price difference on singer.com is about $20.
Owners disagree. Several PatternReview owners call it easy once the color-coded diagram is followed; one found it very hard. Threading is manual lay-in with no air system.

faqs.q: Can it do a rolled hem?
faqs.a: Yes, the rolled hem is built in. One owner reported not being able to get it to work.

faqs.q: Does it have a free arm?
faqs.a: Yes, a built-in free arm for cuffs and sleeves.
Singer 2022 serger needles, equivalent to ELx705, in sizes 80/12 and 90/14.
13.5 lb per the Amazon listing; 14 x 11 x 11.5 in with the thread stand down.

faqs.q: What is the differential feed range?
faqs.a: 0.7 to 2.0 per the Amazon listing. Stitch length is 2.0 to 4.0 mm and cutting width 3.0 to 6.7 mm.

faqs.q: Is it better than the Brother 1034D?
faqs.a: It adds 2-thread stitches and a free arm; the Brother is praised for a brighter light and easier threading. Both run 1,300 spm with differential feed.
Singer's warranty page states 25 years on the head, 2 years on motor and electrical parts and 90 days on adjustments and attachments.
